title: Leakages and injections
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank card teaches the same leakages and injections idea but is pitched at VCE Units 1 and 2 depth, with five sectors and capital-goods detail, and frames the effect as spending rising or falling rather than growth, so a new point suits the Years 9 and 10 brief better.

draft.title: Leakages and injections
card: Money taken out of the circular flow, so it is not spent on Australian goods and services. The three leakages are saving, tax and imports.
Money added to the circular flow. The three injections are investment (businesses buying equipment and buildings), government spending and exports.
Each leakage has a matching injection. Saving is paired with investment, tax with government spending, and imports with exports.
If injections are greater than leakages, more money flows through the economy and it grows. If leakages are greater than injections, the flow shrinks.
draft.remember: Leakages take money out of the flow. Injections put it in. Injections above leakages mean growth.

a.q: A household in Geelong puts $500 of its pay into a savings account. In the circular flow, what is this?
opts: A leakage, because the money is not spent
An injection, because the bank gets money
A leakage, because the money is paid as tax
An injection, because the household gets interest
a.why: Saved money is taken out of the flow of spending, so saving is a leakage. It is not an injection: the bank holding the money does not add new spending to the flow.
a.clue: Is the $500 being spent on goods and services?

b.q: In one year, the total of injections in Australia is greater than the total of leakages. What is the most likely result?
opts: More money flows through the economy, so it grows
Less money flows through the economy, so it shrinks
The flow stays the same, as the two always cancel out
Households save more, so spending falls
b.why: Injections add money to the flow and leakages remove it. When injections are larger, the flow gets bigger and the economy grows. The shrinking option reverses this and describes leakages above injections.
b.clue: Which of the two adds money to the flow?

a.best: A leakage, because the money is not spent

b.best: More money flows through the economy, so it grows
